title: From Exact Diagonalization to DMRG: A Complete Numerical Study of the Transverse-Field Ising Model
abstract: We present a self-contained numerical study of the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model (TFIM), tracing its ground-state entanglement structure from exact diagonalization at small system size (L=8,14,20) through density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations up to L=100. A single, consistent methodology - identical field grid, identical convergence diagnostic (independent runs at bond dimensions chi=100 and chi=200 at every point) - is used across all seven system sizes, and we show explicitly where exact diagonalization and DMRG must agree exactly rather than merely approximately. Along the way we document and resolve a bond-dimension convergence artifact that produced a spurious discontinuity in an earlier, less systematic dataset, as a worked cautionary example for practitioners. Using the resolved dataset we extract the central charge of the transition via two complementary routes - the leading logarithmic finite-size scaling of the mid-chain entropy, and the full Calabrese-Cardy formula applied to every bond of every system size simultaneously - obtaining c_eff to 0.51-0.52 as short-distance lattice corrections are systematically excluded, consistent with the exact two-dimensional Ising value c=1/2. We review the quantum-classical (Suzuki-Trotter) correspondence that underlies this agreement and discuss how the Widom-Kadanoff scaling hypothesis transplants from the classical to the quantum problem. The manuscript is intended as both a physics result and a worked methodological example of careful finite-size numerics.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive numerical investigation into the 1D Transverse-Field Ising Model, comparing results from Exact Diagonalization and DMRG across multiple system sizes. By employing rigorous consistency checks, the authors successfully extract the central charge of the critical point, confirming its theoretical value of $c=1/2$. The work serves as an important methodological guide for practitioners in quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: To conduct a complete numerical study of the ground-state entanglement structure of the 1D Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM) and extract its central charge.
main_result: The effective central charge ($c_{	ext{eff}}$) was found to converge robustly to $0.51-0.52$, consistent with the exact theoretical value of $c=1/2$ expected for 2D Ising universality class.
method: The study systematically compares results from Exact Diagonalization (ED) on small systems and Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) up to large sizes, using identical convergence diagnostics across all calculations.
model_or_system: The system is the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model (TFIM), described by the Hamiltonian $H = -\sum_i J \sigma^z_i \sigma^z_{i+1} - h \sum_i \sigma^x_i$. The phase transition occurs at a critical field $h_c=1$.
key_observables: Bipartite entanglement entropy ($S(l)$), mid-chain entanglement entropy ($S_{mid}$), and the effective central charge ($	ext{c}_{	ext{eff}}$).
important_parameters: System size $L$ (up to 100), transverse field $h$, and DMRG bond dimension $\chi$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on systematic convergence checks across multiple numerical methods, explicitly resolving artifacts caused by finite-size effects or insufficient bond dimensions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mid-chain entanglement entropy vs. field for various $L$, show full bond-by-bond profiles collapsing onto a single curve using the Calabrese-Cardy variable, and plot $	ext{c}_{	ext{eff}}$ showing convergence to $1/2$.
paper_structure: The paper is structured as both a physical result and a methodological guide, detailing the numerical progression from small ED calculations to large DMRG simulations, culminating in the extraction of critical exponents via entropy scaling.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous benchmark for applying advanced tensor network methods (DMRG) by demonstrating how systematic convergence checks can resolve spurious numerical artifacts and confirm fundamental theoretical predictions regarding quantum criticality.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

Figure 2: Entanglement entropy S(l) vs. bond index l, L = 100, for seven representative fields spanning both phases and the transition.
Figure 3: Entanglement entropy landscape S(l, h), L = 100, over the full sampled field range.
Figure 4: Entanglement entropy vs. the full Calabrese-Cardy variable, all bonds, all seven system sizes, at h = 1.
